# Issue #7: touching intervals are not merged

`merge_intervals([(1, 3), (3, 5)])` returns `[(1, 3), (3, 5)]` but the documented
behaviour is that closed intervals sharing an endpoint merge into `[(1, 5)]`.
Unsorted input must also be handled. Fix `ranges/merge.py`.

arguments.summary: Fixed `ranges/merge.py` with two changes: (1) the merge condition was `start < last_end`, which failed to merge touching intervals like (1,3) and (3,5); changed to `start <= last_end` so closed intervals sharing an endpoint merge. (2) The function assumed sorted input; now it sorts all intervals (as tuples) before merging, so unsorted input is handled correctly. Both existing tests pass, plus manual checks for unsorted, contained, and empty inputs.
